classification.difficultyReason: Form an equation from adjacent angles on a straight line, collect like terms and solve.

spec.description: Horizontal straight line and a ray rising right from an interior point. The left upper angle is labelled x degrees and the right upper angle is labelled (x−100) degrees. No arcs or arrowheads. Decorative blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled adjacent angles form a straight angle, so x+(x−100)=180. Schematic ray inclination supplies no numerical angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original algebraic angle labels are visible; no solution values appear.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}x+(x-100)&=180\\2x-100&=180\\2x&=280\\x&=140\end{align*}$$

Check: the angles are $140^{\circ}$ and $40^{\circ}$, and $140^{\circ}+40^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$.
